regulatoryStatus.note: CORRECTED. The openfda.generic_name:"exenatide" query returns only TWO applications; querying products.brand_name reveals two more. Full fetched picture: Bydureon NDA022200 (AP 2012-01-27) and Bydureon BCise NDA209210 (AP 2017-10-20) are Discontinued; the original AstraZeneca Byetta NDA021773 (AP 2005-04-28) is Discontinued; a second Byetta application NDA021919 (sponsor AMYLIN, AP 2009-10-30) is still Prescription; generic synthetic exenatide ANDA206697 (Amneal, AP 2024-11-19) is Prescription. Do NOT write that exenatide was withdrawn, and do NOT write that all brands remain available. The extended-release (Bydureon) form specifically is discontinued.

negativeOrNullFindings: PMID 39919773 is the single most important citation here: a phase 3 trial that failed to reproduce the widely-reported phase 2 Parkinson's signal (PMID 28781108). Any exenatide page that mentions neuroprotection without this is out of date.
PMID 29246950 (SUSTAIN 3) - exenatide ER was beaten by semaglutide.
PMIDs 18450614 and 18456920 are the pancreatitis-era safety correspondence.
cautions: Do not state that Byetta or Bydureon are currently marketed without re-checking openFDA marketing_status - the fetched record shows Discontinued for the branded products.
DURATION and AWARD are different programmes (exenatide vs dulaglutide) - do not cross them.
couldNotConfirm: Whether the Amylin-sponsored Byetta application NDA021919 corresponds to a product physically on the market today; openFDA marketing_status reflects the application record, not shelf availability.
